body:
## Problem

A blank line before the Content-Length header makes header parsing fail with "Content-Length not found in header". An LF in the 'name' state falls through to the 'invalid' state, which only return to 'name' at the *next* LF. That LF terminates the next line, so the line with Content-Length is swallowed.
The same issue happens when a junk line is a prefix of the header name (e.g. "cont\nContent-Length: ...").

## Solution

When seeing an LF in the 'name' state, reset the cursor and stay in 'name' rather than entering 'invalid'.

comment_data.body:
Ah, I see how my sentence was a bit misleading.
The point here is that the text on previous line is a prefix of the string "Context-Length"

For example `"Cont\nContent-Length:..."` where "Cont" is a prefix of "Content-Length".

Previous logic will skip "Content-Length: ..." hence failing to parse the header.

comment_regular_data.body: Some servers print log output to stdout, mixing logs into communication messages. This PR seems to improve our tolerance for these junk messages (and the current code also has some similar handling). LGTM.

@justinmk I applied both changes. Also updated the wording in the commit message.
The 2 failures previously in the CI didn't seem relevant to my PR.
